azimuthal_integrate — DRIVE pxrd op

• Data kinds: image2d × table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.azimuthal_integrate(image, geometry, n_bins=None, two_theta_range=None, mask=None, solid_angle=True, polarization=None, chi_range=None, supersample=2, memory_budget=None) (to call the implementation directly, import pxrd; pxrd.azimuthal_integrate(image, geometry, n_bins=None, two_theta_range=None, mask=None, solid_angle=True, polarization=None, chi_range=None, supersample=2, memory_budget=None); from the registry, opsdrive.get("azimuthal_integrate"))

Usage

Reduces a 2-D detector image to a 1-D profile in 2θ (azimuthal integration, with mask and corrections).

Each pixel is split into supersample² sub-pixels (value divided equally), distributed into bins by the 2θ at the sub-pixel centre, and averaged per bin (reduces stripes caused by the coarseness of pixel splitting). solid_angle=True divides out the relative solid angle, and if polarization is a number (0 = unpolarised, 1 = horizontally polarised) the polarisation factor, before averaging. mask excludes pixels that are True (bool of the same shape). chi_range = (χ₀, χ₁) [deg] integrates only a sector (χ is the (−180, 180] of atan2). Non-finite pixels are rejected unless they are in the mask.

The default for n_bins is the number giving a width of half the angle of one pixel (0.5·pixel/distance [rad]). Return value (dict): two_theta (bin centres [deg]), intensity (mean), count (sum of sub-pixel weights; bins with 0 have intensity nan —— not filled), sigma (standard error of the mean assuming Poisson).

Raises ValueError: not 2-D, mask shape mismatch, non-finite pixels, empty range, empty sector, number of bins < 8.
